questions.q: What does Yahweh see when he wants to heal Israel?
questions.a: He sees how sinfully the people of Ephraim act and all of the evil things that the people of the city of Samaria do.
Yahweh remembered every evil thing that they do.

questions.q: How did the people make the king glad?
questions.a: The people of Israel please their king by doing evil things.

questions.q: What does Yahweh compare the people to?
questions.a: He compares them to adulterers because they are unfaithful to him.

questions.q: What happened to the king on the day of his festival?
questions.a: The officials made him drunk with wine until he became sick, and he joined with those who mock Yahweh.

questions.q: What were the people’s hearts like?
questions.a: Their hearts were as hot with anger as the heat of an oven.

questions.q: What happened to all the kings of Israel?
questions.a: All of their kings died violently; yet none of them called out to Yahweh for help.
Ephraim has become ruined because of his alliances with foreign nations.

questions.q: What did the people not realize was happening to them?
questions.a: Foreigners have drained away their resources and their nation is becoming powerless yet the people of Israel do not realize it.

questions.q: What have the people of Israel not done despite everything that has happened?
questions.a: They have not returned to worship Yahweh their God or tried to know him.

questions.q: What made Ephraim like a dove?
questions.a: Ephraim was as foolish and stupid as a dove because they asked other nations instead of Yahweh to help them.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do to them?
questions.a: He will not allow them to succeed but instead will punish them.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh not rescue the people?
questions.a: Yahweh did not rescue the people because they spoke lies against him.

questions.q: What did the people do instead of crying out to Yahweh for help?
questions.a: They just lie on their beds and wail.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he did for the people?
questions.a: He trained them and made them strong.

questions.q: Why will the officials die in battle?
questions.a: The officials will die in battle because what they said made Yahweh very angry.

commentary.text: The manifold sins of Israel. (Hos. 7:1-7) Their senselessness and hypocrisy. (Hos. 7:8-16)

Hos. 7:1-7 A practical disbelief of God's government was at the bottom of all israel's wickedness; as if God could not see it or did not heed it. Their sins appear on every side of them. Their hearts were inflamed by evil desires, like a heated oven. In the midst of their troubles as a nation, the people never thought of seeking help from God. The actual wickedness of men's lives bears a very small proportion to what is in their hearts. But when lust is inwardly cherished, it will break forth into outward sin. Those who tempt others to drunkenness never can be their real friends, and often design their ruin. Thus men execute the Divine vengeance on each other. Those are not only heated with sin, but hardened in sin, who continue to live without prayer, even when in trouble and distress.

Hos. 7:8-16 Israel was as a cake not turned, half burnt and half dough, none of it fit for use; a mixture of idolatry and of the worship of Jehovah. There were tokens of approaching ruin, as grey hairs are of old age, but they noticed them not. The pride which leads to break the law of God leads to self-flattery. The mercy and grace of God are the only refuge to which obstinate sinners never think of fleeing. Though they may howl forth their terrors in the form of prayers, they seldom cry to God with their hearts. Even their prayers for earthly mercies only seek fuel for their lusts. Their turning from one sect, sentiment, form, or vice, to another, still leaves them far short of Christ and holiness. Such are we by nature. And such shall we prove if left to ourselves. Create in us a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within us.
